trigger_signals: A specific interaction (click, type, scroll, route change) feels slow or janky and needs a trace-backed explanation
Component-level rendering, long tasks, hydration or animation frame drops must be measured on a frozen journey

anti_add.text: Measure field Core Web Vitals, including field INP, for a page

guidance: Default budgets when the user supplies none: long task <= 50 ms, frame <= 16.7 ms (60 fps), interaction latency (INP) <= 200 ms at p75; report every measured value against them and say when a default was used.

Hypothesis catalog: animating width/height/top/left instead of transform/opacity triggers layout and paint; a parent CSS variable driving child transforms recalculates every child; Framer Motion x/y/scale shorthands run on the main thread and drop frames under load.
Ownership: field INP belongs to web-performance-diagnostics; this Skill owns component-level interaction traces.
Ownership: component-level render and interaction traces belong here; page-level Core Web Vitals, including field INP, belong to web-performance-diagnostics.

trigger_signals: A Kubernetes workload needs a read-only go/no-go before deployment covering rollout, scaling, policy and rollback
Manifests or a cluster must be checked against AKS Automatic or platform safeguards before anything is applied
guidance: Severity taxonomy per issue: incompatible (migration blocker), requiresChanges, autoFixed by the platform, cluster-config. Order blockers first; group by constraint id when more than 10 issues.
Per-issue record: constraint id, severity, affected namespace/resource (Kind), current value, required value, fix summary, documentation link.
AKS Automatic variant: check container resource requests and limits, probes, non-root and privilege settings, and disallowed host access against the safeguard constraints.

Give concrete rollout values when the plan lacks them (for example maxUnavailable 0, maxSurge 1, replica count, PodDisruptionBudget minAvailable, HPA bounds) and compute rollback cost arithmetic explicitly.
outputs_add: per-issue severity record with current and required values

procedure_insert.text: Return concrete recommended values for rollout strategy, autoscaling and disruption budgets, each with its arithmetic, instead of naming the topic only.

resolves.kubernetes-deployment-readiness#F1: fixed: guidance + outputs_add (severity taxonomy, blocker-first, per-issue record); Phase D loss reasons (concrete values, rollback arithmetic) addressed by procedure_insert

trigger_signals: A test or job fails intermittently and needs a reproducible failure model before anyone edits code
Retries, timeouts, ordering or cleanup may be masking a race, leaked state or an arbitrary sleep
inputs: An observed nondeterministic or resilience failure with reproduction context: the failing test or job, logs, environment, and any suspected cause (invalid data, race, contamination, fragile wait).
guidance: First-class hypothesis: an arbitrary sleep or fixed timeout. Prefer condition-based waiting (poll for the specific state with a bounded timeout and a failure message naming the expected and last observed state) over longer sleeps.
When the cause is invalid data, recommend validation at four layers: entry point, business logic, environment guard, and debug instrumentation.
Deliver the concrete fix as a patch or code block for the owner to apply; do not withhold it as a vague candidate when the race is confirmed, and state exactly what remains unverified.

Preserve existing approved timezone and business semantics. A proposed policyholder-zone change is a separate product decision, not an assumed implementation fix. Reproduction and repeat checks must use the unchanged semantics until that decision is approved.

procedure_insert.text: List the candidate causes including arbitrary sleeps or fixed timeouts, and rank them by the evidence from the repeated runs.

resolves.resilience-and-determinism#F1: fixed: inputs replaced (observed failure, not pre-confirmed cause)
resolves.resilience-and-determinism#F2: fixed: guidance + procedure_insert (sleep hypothesis, condition-based waiting)

trigger_signals: A page or journey needs a page-load, network, caching or Core Web Vitals baseline under declared conditions
Someone asks why a page is slow and needs waterfall, asset and bundle evidence rather than one Lighthouse score

anti_add.text: Trace one slow interaction or component render in an already loaded page

guidance: Core Web Vitals thresholds at p75: LCP good <= 2.5 s, poor > 4 s; INP good <= 200 ms, poor > 500 ms; CLS good <= 0.1, poor > 0.25. Label every number as lab or field data and never mix them in one verdict.

Detect the framework and bundler from config files and package.json, then attribute large bundles to owning packages and check tree-shaking (sideEffects, usedExports, production mode) before proposing hypotheses.

Ownership: field and lab INP, LCP, CLS and other Core Web Vitals belong here; component-level interaction traces belong to frontend-rendering-and-interaction-performance.
outputs_add: threshold table with lab or field label per metric
